"fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/problem "Use the substitution $u=x^{3} + 1$. Which integral is obtained?

$$
\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=x^{3} + 1$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 2^{x^{3} + 1} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

The transformed integral is

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$"] [:db/add "fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "fe01eccb-793a-59d6-a00c-81c9b20ac1cd" :question/answer-fields
